records.title: items.Ancestors walks the parent chain one query at a time
records.body:
`internal/items/items.go:122-144`. `Ancestors` fetches the item, then loops `for item.ParentID != nil`, calling `s.ItemByID(ctx, *item.ParentID)` once per level. One round trip per ancestor, plus the initial `Get`.

**This is not urgent and nobody should panic about it.** The chain is bounded at three by the scanner's own key scheme (`episode` → `season` → `series`; a movie has none), so it is at most four queries, and `Ancestors` has two callers — `internal/server/library/ancestors.go:13` on `GetAncestors`, and `internal/metadata/metadata.go:96` once per item in an identify batch. Neither is hot.

Worth recording rather than fixing now because the bound is incidental. The loop is written to handle arbitrary depth — it even carries a `seen` map to survive a cycle — so it will keep working, quietly, if a collection or box-set hierarchy ever nests deeper than the three levels the scanner writes today. The metadata batch is where that would first be felt: `batchSize` items × depth round trips inside a step that is already rate-limited against a provider.

If it does need fixing, the shape is one recursive CTE up `parent_id` in the way `internal/items/nextup.go` already drops to raw SQL for `DISTINCT ON`, rather than an eager load — `WithParent` only reaches one level and would have to be nested to the depth in advance.

Hi Skeptic, thanks for the great plugin. Usability wise, it would be really helpful to able to export the co-citations table as a plain node/edge list or adjacency matrix (either for the local note or the global graph). (Or maybe even cooler, extracting hierarchies from flat notes by applying breadth first search or other spanning tree algorithms to the edge list)

records.title: Infinite loop with recursive JSR
records.body:
Yes, I realize that the bytecode is technically illegal because of the recursive JSR, but when decompiling a JAR if an unused class contains this sequence then the entire decompilation will halt.

If you decide that this is out of scope I respect that decision. However, I do feel that this should be fixed

``` java
.method public static main : ([Ljava/lang/String;)V 
    .code stack 1024 locals 10
    jsr L1
L1:
    jsr L2
    jsr L1
    return
L2:
    astore_1
    pop
    ret 1
    .end code 
.end method 
```
